question: A 58-year-old male with a history of congestive heart failure and hypertension comes to you with the chief complaint of new-onset cough as well as increased serum potassium in the setting of a new medication. Which of the following medications is most likely responsible for these findings?
analysis: The new-onset cough and increased serum potassium in a patient with congestive heart failure and hypertension suggest the possibility of drug-induced side effects. Among the options provided, the medication most likely responsible for these findings is Lisinopril, an ACE inhibitor commonly associated with cough as a side effect and can also lead to hyperkalemia.
